verdict.justification: Both deliverables correctly identify and resolve the critical workspace governance conflict—rejecting the unapproved 'Purchase team alone' rule from proposal-r3 in favor of the governing record-r2 requiring Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams for price change approvals. However, Deliverable A is significantly more comprehensive, detailed, and realistic as a senior procurement manager's blueprint. In its Modular Quotation Structure (Section 3), A thoughtfully includes base architecture, conversion & overheads, and one-time tooling/homologation costs (M1, M6, M7) alongside the four prompted categories, whereas B only lists the four prompted categories and awkwardly lumps tooling into aesthetic design elements. Furthermore, A's post-nomination change matrix (Section 5) explicitly requires TRSO update sign-offs (ER, Quality, Purchase) across every change class, whereas B's Section 4 table omits the TRSO sign-off step and has a contradiction between its C0 definition ('no re-quote', 'recorded and notified') and its flexibility levers. Finally, Deliverable A provides a much better structured technical blueprint for TechSol (Section 6), breaking requirements down into a clear table covering core data objects, workflow engine, supplier portal, cost engine, e-signatures, audit, dashboards, and integrations.
